label: Clabber
note: Came to the American South with the Ulster Scots and was once used as a quick leavener before baking powder; making it virtually stopped once milk was pasteurised

about.text: Clabber is a type of soured milk. It is produced by allowing unpasteurized milk to turn sour (ferment) at a specific humidity and temperature. Over time, the milk thickens or curdles into a yogurt-like consistency with a strong, sour flavor. According to Joy of Cooking, "Clabber... is milk that has soured to the stage of a firm curd but not to a separation of the whey."

how.label: sour raw milk
how.text: Raw milk is left to sour by its own bacteria until it sets into a firm curd but before whey separates. Pasteurisation kills those bacteria, so clabber has largely disappeared.
